extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers interested in ethics, social reform, and literary essays (late 19th/early 20th-century audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A popular-sermon / essay that proposes a modernized, experience-based code of ethics and argues for social reforms (notably specialization in domestic and maternal work). It mixes prescriptive commandments with justificatory argument and illustrative anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: clearer conception of right and wrong based on knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a sermon. Its purpose is to point out the need of a clearer conception of right and wrong, based on knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author intends a code grounded in inquiry and experience rather than unexamined authority; the sermon is presented as a starting point for study and reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical method: seek and search out by wisdom; base ethics on plain facts
rubrics_metrics.description: We must 'give our hearts to seek and search out by wisdom ...' and base a farther code of ethics on the plain facts of common experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject taking other people's judgment or mere authoritative pronouncement; ethics should be tested, proven by observation of consequences, and open to alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative gradation of wrongness (discriminate among sins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some things are much more wrong than others; experience teaches us to discriminate in our judgment of right and wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat all prohibitions as equal; evaluate by consequences and social harm rather than simply by textual commandment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of ethical guidance: instructions, not authoritative commands
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not want commands, we want instructions; we want to know why things are wrong, which are the most wrong, and what are their respective consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical teaching should explain reasons and relative harms in language a bright child can understand and a practical person respect; avoid priestly/parodic authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics orientation: social first, personal later
rubrics_metrics.description: The old ethics is wholly personal, the new ethics (still unwritten) is social first--personal later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize duties and standards that protect and promote social welfare and collective service rather than exclusively personal piety or personal prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 1. Thou shalt learn that human love is a natural law and obey it as the main condition of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt learn that human love is a natural law and obey it as the main condition of life: the service of man is the worship of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the first and primary principle; frames love/service to others as the core ethical foundation rather than ritual or isolated prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 2. Thou shalt learn that the first duty is to find thy work and do it
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt learn that the first duty of human life is to find thy work and do it; for by labor ye live and grow and in it is worship, pride and joy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes productive labor and the ethical importance of contributing through meaningful work; links work to personal development and social service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 3. Thou shalt keep an open mind and use it
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt keep an open mind and use it, welcoming new knowledge and new truth and giving them to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates intellectual openness, sharing discoveries and progress as an ethical duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 4. Thou shalt maintain liberty and justice for everyone
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt maintain liberty and justice for everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms political and legal equality as ethical imperatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 5. Thou shalt maintain thy health and thy chastity
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt maintain thy health and thy chastity. Temperance and purity are required of all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for personal self-care and temperance as social duties; framed broadly as health and moral restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 6. Thou shalt not lie, break faith or cheat
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not lie, break faith or cheat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condemns dishonesty, breach of trust, and cheating; substitutes specific modern phrasing for older formulations about oaths/perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 7. Thou shalt not gamble, nor live idly on the labor of others, nor by any usury
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not gamble, nor live idly on the labor of others, nor by any usury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies gambling and parasitic economic behavior as major social evils absent from ancient codes; links economic morality to social health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 8. Thou shalt not steal; nor take from one another save in fair exchange or as a free gift
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not steal; nor take from one another save in fair exchange or as a free gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaffirms property norms but specifies fairness and voluntary transfer as the ethical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 9. Thou shalt not do unnecessary hurt to any living thing
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not do unnecessary hurt to any living thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General prohibition against gratuitous harm; expands moral concern to living creatures beyond humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Suggestions — 10. Thou shalt not worship the past nor be content with the present; growth is the law of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not worship the past nor be content with the present, for growth is the law of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages progress, rejects conservatism that fetters improvement; frames ethical duty as active advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirement: accessible exposition for child and practical man
rubrics_metrics.description: We want an exposition which a bright child can understand and a practical man respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical codes and arguments should use clear, non-technical language and give practical reasons and examples; avoid obscure theological language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid replacing Divine Command: auxiliary, not substitute to Ten Commandments
rubrics_metrics.description: These are auxiliary and merely suggestive of study; the Ten (Commandments) stand as before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new suggestions are proposed as complementary, not as sacrilegious replacements of established religious precepts; useful for pragmatic reformers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow specialization for development of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: For the development of genius we must allow it to specialize... genius must be allowed to do the work it has a genius for, or none will be manifested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied social principle: individuals should be permitted and encouraged to specialize (in arts, professions, domestic roles when appropriate) so talents can produce maximal social benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic and maternal services require genius, education, and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The domestic and maternal services ... are left to be performed by the average mind, by the average woman, by instinct. For the performance of any social service of importance, three powers are required: first, special ability or genius; second, education; third, experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that housework and child care should benefit from specialization and professional training (not merely instinct), because early childhood is crucial and current unpaid/unspecialized provision harms children and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching as specialized motherhood and social motherhood value
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching is a form of specialized motherhood... The teacher is to some degree a social mother, and the advantage of this social motherhood is so great that it would seem impossible to question it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevates teaching as professionalized child-caring that spreads the advantages of civilization; implies policy/value rubric to honor and properly remunerate such specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for institutional/support solutions rather than private hiring alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Some say 'the mother should engage this specialist to help her in the home,' or 'the mother must be taught.' But 'who is to teach her?' 'Who understands this work?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical constraint: private hiring or ad-hoc training is insufficient; social institutions, public statutes, and a cadre of high-quality specialists are required to raise child welfare broadly.
